business_scope.primary_industry_name: Deep-Sea Tugboat Towage and Maritime Emergency Salvage Contracts

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (unitary national jurisdiction with no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Kingdom of Spain on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed in Beijing on 26 November 2005; entered into force on 1 July 2008)

Convention between the Kingdom of Spain and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (signed on 22 November 1990; entered into force on 1 January 1992)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital; Real Decreto 1784/1996, de 19 de julio, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento del Registro Mercantil; Implementing Directive (EU) 2018/843 as transposed by Spanish law; UBO registration is administrated by the Banco de España, CNMV, and SEPBLAC in their respective supervisory scopes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificado Negativo de Denominación Social (negative name clearance certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic issuance; no apostille required for domestic SL incorporation; original must be presented to the Spanish notary within its statutory validity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) including the corporate bylaws (estatutos)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish notary (Notaría) at the chosen corporate domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only if the deed needs to be legalized for use outside Spain; domestic registration requires filing of the notarial protocol with the Commercial Registry, not an apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (poder notarial) granted by foreign incorporators or directors to the Spanish incorporation counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin, e.g., a notarial office in the People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if originating jurisdiction is party to the 1961 Hague Convention) followed by sworn translation into Spanish; otherwise Spanish consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) certificate for non-resident foreign directors/shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of the Interior (Dirección General de la Policía) through Spanish consulates or Comisaría General de Extranjería y Fronteras
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The NIE certificate itself is a domestic Spanish administrative document; supporting foreign identity documents must be apostilled or consular legalized and translated by a sworn translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Evidence of right to use the registered office address (proof of ownership, lease, or virtual office service agreement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Property owner / virtual office service provider / notarized rental agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille is required for domestic use; if property deed is issued abroad, apostille or consular legalization and sworn translation are required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, shareholders holding more than 25%, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (ii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, (iv) the Bank of Spain and SEPBLAC supervisory warning lists, and (v) Spanish criminal record and PEP registers. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory whenever a PEP is identified, as required by Article 15 of Ley 10/2010. The screening results must be documented and retained for the statutory AML record-keeping period.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), electronic application channel administered by the Colegio de Registradores de España; the official name application is obtained through the 'Nombre' service available at www.registradores.org and rmc.registradores.org
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All proposed corporate names must be drafted in Spanish. Foreign-language names are permissible only when transliterated or rendered in Latin-alphabet characters that uphold the Spanish phonetic and orthographic system. The name must be distinctive and cannot create confusion with existing registered names. The corporate type designation 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'S.L.' must follow the chosen distinctive name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Mercantil Central issues a negative rejection of the requested denomination, the applicant may file a recurso de alzada before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of Justice within one month from notification. The DGSJFP must resolve within three months; a resolution not issued within that period is deemed a rejection for appeal-purposes. The applicant may alternatively re-enter the name clearance queue with a new proposed name or request an updated certification for a variant. No extension of a valid negative certification is permitted after the 60-day period has expired; a fresh certificate must be requested.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible at the company-law level: an SL may formally use a virtual office as its registered address if it has a demonstrable right to use the address for service of process and official notifications. However, ISIC 5222 deep-sea towage and maritime emergency salvage operations require a maritime operator license from the Dirección General de la Marina Mercante (DGMM). That license requires an operational shore-based office and emergency response facility in Spain; a mail-forwarding or virtual office alone does not constitute sufficient commercial substance for maritime license approval.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-elevated risk; estimated 25% probability per operating year of an unannounced physical inspection by DGMM port-state control, SEPBLAC for AML compliance, or the Commercial Registry for registered-office verification. The risk increases during the first year after incorporation because of the maritime safety supervision regime.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Negative corporate name clearance (certificado negativo de denominación social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Colegio de Registradores
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff fixed by Spanish ministerial fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation, minutes, bylaws review, and notarial protocol
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff (Arancel Notarial) based on the share capital and document length

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Inscription of the SL in the Provincial Commercial Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory commercial registry tariff (Arancel del Registro Mercantil)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and consular legalization of foreign incorporation documents, passports, and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice / Ministry of Foreign Affairs, consular post, and authorized apostille office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official per-document apostille and consular fee schedule, escalated for expedited service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of foreign public documents into Spanish (traducción jurada)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (traductor jurado) appointed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-page market benchmark accepted by the Commercial Registry; regulated by the professional association fee guidelines

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE (foreigner identification number) application for non-resident incorporators or directors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish consulate or Comisaría General de Extranjería y Fronteras
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee and administrative fee under Tasa 790-062, official government fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, EU sanctions, and AML/CFT screening pack for all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External compliance provider / law firm performing enhanced due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual PEP and sanctions screening subscription per person plus per-case EDD review; prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal advisory and incorporation counsel fees for SL constitution, statutory compliance, and drafting of articles of association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee market benchmark for cross-border incorporation of an SL with non-resident corporate shareholders

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), particularly Articles 22 (minimum capital), 23 (public deed), 24-31 (subscription and payment), 113 (registered office), and 124-127 (administrators).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) and Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for name certification
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) to be filed with the Registro Mercantil Provincial, followed by publication in the Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The registered capital of an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) must be at least EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in at incorporation. The capital may be paid in cash (bank deposit certificate issued by a Spanish credit institution) or in kind (valued by an independent expert report when non-cash). The funds must remain in escrow in an account opened in the company's name at the time of incorporation and are only released after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned incorporators, acting as the initial board, resolve: (1) to irrevocably subscribe all 3,000 shares of the social capital in accordance with the Escritura de Constitución, each fully paid-up; (2) to adopt the registered office at Calle Alcalá, 27, Madrid, Spain; (3) to appoint the Sole Administrator, Mr. Alejandro Vidal, who accepts the office; (4) to ratify the opening of the corporate bank account and the filing of the tax identification number application; (5) to authorize the administrator to complete all statutory filings and to register the company with the Mercantile Registry. This resolution is passed unanimously and enters into force immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certified Name Approval from the Central Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry, Ministry of Justice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application through the official site www.registradores.org or the Ministry of Justice electronic portal requesting, for a fee, a negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación) for the proposed corporate name 'ES SL Towage and Salvage, S.L.'. The request must include up to three alternative names in descending priority. After approval, the name is reserved for a non-extendable period of 6 months, which must cover the entire incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Application form for name certification (solicitud de certificación negativa de denominación)
Corporate identification of the promoters (DNI, NIE or passport)
Payment receipt of official fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the request is denied because of identical or confusingly similar names, the applicant must resubmit with new alternative names. If the registry fails to respond within 5 days, a consecutive preliminary certificate can be obtained by requesting a waiver or applying for a new name to avoid expiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Escrow Bank Account and Deposit of Minimum Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit entity (bank or savings bank) licensed by Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account in the name of 'ES SL Towage and Salvage, S.L.' (pending inscription). Deposit the full minimum capital of EUR 3,000 plus any additional capital decided by the promoters. Obtain from the bank an original certificate of capital deposit (certificado de desembolso) stating the account holder's name, account number, and the exact amount deposited, dated no earlier than six months prior to the execution of the public deed.
required_dossiers: Signed internal account opening request by all subscribing partners
DNI/NIE/passport of each promoter
Draft of the articles of association to identify the corporate name and registered office
Initial deposit of at least EUR 3,000
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account opening due to anti-money laundering identification issues, submit the missing documentation or choose another credit entity. The capital deposit certificate must be reissued if it expires before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Public Deed of Incorporation before a Spanish Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario (Spanish Public Notary) within the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a notary of the selected collegiate district with the full draft of the Escritura de Constitución and the Bylaws (estatutos). The notary will verify legal capacity, the name certificate, the bank deposit certificate, and the contribution of the partners. Execute the public deed, which must include the statutory clauses, share capital division, registered office, administration structure, and the annual account closing date. Pay notarial fees. After execution, the notary will send the telematic copy to the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: Certified negative name certificate
Bank certificate evidencing paid-up capital
Draft of the Escritura de Constitución and statutes
DNI/NIE/passport of each founding partner or their representative powers
NIF of the entity if previously assigned (e.g., provisional or if fully constituted by public deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises legal defects (e.g., non-compliance with capital payment rules or invalid clauses), amend the draft and re-execute. If the notary refuses due to the absence of an essential document, complete the dossier and rerequest appointment; fees are generally reducible if a new deed supersedes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Delegación de Grandes Contribuyentes or provincial tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Model 036 form (censo de obligados tributarios) together with a copy of the public deed of incorporation and the identity of the legal representative. The AEAT will issue a provisional NIF (unless already issued by the notary through the telematics channel). This NIF is required to complete registration and to enable the company to begin operations under the corporate name. The definitive NIF is issued after the mercantile registration is recorded.
required_dossiers: Model 036 form (declaración censal de alta)
Copy of the public deed of incorporation
DNI/NIE/passport of the legal representative
Power of attorney if the filing is done by a third party
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried due to inconsistency in the deed or representative powers, rectify the Model 036 and resubmit electronically. The provisional NIF may be validated immediately; otherwise, request a face-to-face appointment at the AEAT office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Company in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) of the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 2 months from the date of the public deed, submit a certified copy of the deed and the supporting documents for registration. The registry will examine the legality, capacity, and statutory consistency of the deed. Once approved, the company acquires legal personality and the inscription is communicated electronically to the BORME and the AEAT for the definitive NIF. Pay the registration fee and the BORME publication fee.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the public deed of incorporation
First board resolution (if required by the deed)
Proof of deposit of capital (bank certificate, already in deed)
Documentation evidencing names, NIFs, and appointments of administrators
Solicitud de inscripción (Modelo oficial del Registro)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect or negative note, correct the deed or complete the missing legal requirements and resubmit within the statutory time; before the end of the two-month deadline, file an application for extension arguing force majeure or legal impossibility. Obtain a new name certificate if the reserved name expired.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mandatory Publication in BORME and Post-Registration Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME) – Spain's Official Gazette of the Mercantile Registry; Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the registry automatically transmits to BORME for publication of the company incorporation notice, including the general data of the company, registered capital, and administrator details. In parallel, the legal representative must obtain a definitive NIF, register the company with the provincial tax office (Modelo 036 updated), and obtain the corporate seal and social security employer registration (Código de Cuenta de Cotización) if employees will be hired.
required_dossiers: Copy of the registration certificate issued by the Mercantile Registry
BORME publication excerpt
NIF final certificate
Modelo 036 update
Protocol of the first board meeting appointing officers if not already in the deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If BORME fails to publish within expected timeline, contact the registry to confirm transmitted data. For the definitive NIF, if the procedure is blocked due to lack of administrative matching, apply for a provisional NIF renewal and maintain regular tax communication with AEAT to avoid penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de la Marina Mercante (General Directorate of the Merchant Marine) under the Spanish Ministry of Transport and Sustainable Mobility (Ministerio de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible), with technical coordination by the Instituto Social de la Marina and state port authorities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Habilitación para la prestación de servicios de remolque y salvamento marítimo (Authorization to provide marine towage and salvage services) – issued as an administrative concession or qualifying license in accordance with Law 14/2014, of 24 July, on Merchant Shipping and Articles 275-276 of the Royal Legislative Decree 2/2011 (State Ports and Merchant Marine Act).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) and the corresponding regional environmental authority of the autonomous community in which the operational base port is located, with the Dirección General de la Marina Mercante for vessel pollution matters
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: For a towage and salvage company operating vessels, the activity is generally classified as Category A.2 of Annex II of Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment (EIA registration required) when the service is auxiliary to port operations; however, if the operation includes shipyards, dry docks, or any land-based industrial facility, the installation may fall under Category A.1 requiring a full EIA report (Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental Ordinaria).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Vessels must comply with the MARPOL 73/78 Protocol as implemented in EU Regulation 2015/757 and Spanish Law 41/2010. Standards include a limit of 15 ppm for oil content in processed bilge water, compliance with Tier III NOx limits in ECAs, a sulfur cap of 0.10% in the Mediterranean Sea and 0.10% in Spanish territorial waters, and waste management plans for hazardous and non-hazardous waste in accordance with Law 7/2022, with all discharges subject to the Merchant Shipping Law and port reception facilities rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory civil defense clearance includes: (1) Fire safety compliance certificate for shore offices and any warehouse or workshop, issued by the competent municipal fire department or regional directorate; (2) Structural load inspection certificate from the colegio of architects or a certified technical engineer for any permanent mooring or lifting equipment; (3) Workplace health and safety registration (modelo de apertura de centro de trabajo) with the regional labor authority, including plans of: evacuation routes, first aid, emergency procedures, and approval of nautical equipment such as towing hooks and winches; (4) Occupational clearance for marine personnel holding valid STCW 78/95 certificates of competency, including GMDSS certification; and (5) Certificate of vessel safety and navigation (certificado de arqueo, condiciones sanitarias, and seguridad de la navegación) issued by the Spanish Ship Inspection service.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Madrid; Online portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); incorporated entities also interact through the Registro Mercantil Central and CIRCE electronic window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated SL: (1) Execute incorporation deed before a Spanish notary, (2) File company registration at the provincial Registro Mercantil obtain the registration certificate, (3) Apply for the definitive NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) at the AEAT local office using standard forms 036/037 or through the CIRCE electronic procedure; provisional NIF (NIF provisional) is granted before registry filing. Non-resident foreign entities deriving Spanish-sourced income or making taxable supplies in Spain must appoint a Spanish tax representative and obtain a non-resident NIF (NIF-N) via Form 036 submitted to AEAT; VAT registration is intrinsic to the NIF application process. The SL's NIF is used for corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades), VAT (IVA), and withholding reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain applies unitary entity-level corporate taxation under Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades; check-the-box fiscal transparency is not available. Relevant elections include: (i) consolidated tax group regime (Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal) under articles 60-70 LIS, requiring the dominant entity to hold at least 75% voting rights, electable by joint filing; (ii) tonnage tax regime (Régimen Especial de Buques y Empresas Navieras, articles 113-117 LIS) available for qualifying ship-owning/operating entities engaged in eligible maritime transport, including towage and salvage, for which corporate tax base is calculated from tonnage; (iii) neutralization of double taxation election for qualifying shareholdings; (iv) VAT group registration election (Régimen Especial del Grupo de Entidades) under articles 163 quindecies - 163 novodecies LIVA; (v) special SME/simplified VAT regimes for small businesses where turnover thresholds are met.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) — Spanish Value Added Tax, governed by Ley 37/1992 (LIVA) and Royal Decree 1624/1992
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic threshold for Spanish VAT registration; any person or entity carrying out taxable supplies of goods or services in Spanish territory, including foreign non-established suppliers performing B2B/B2C services subject to Spanish VAT, must register without reference to turnover. Intra-Union distance sales of goods by non-established EU suppliers are shielded by the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) regime up to EUR 10,000 EU-wide annual turnover threshold; B2C digital/telecom/broadcasting services benefit from the EU VAT mini One-Stop-Shop thresholds. Spanish simplified VAT regime for small enterprises (Régimen Simplificado) is available for certain sectors with turnover below EUR 250,000 (B2B only), not applicable to towage/salvage ISIC 5222 unless expressly covered.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates real-time VAT transaction reporting for large enterprises under SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información de IVA): taxpayers with turnover exceeding EUR 6,010,121.04, or those in consolidated groups or special regime Large Companies, must submit electronic VAT registers to AEAT within 4 business days from issue/receipt via its web services (SOAP/REST API with digital certificate authentication). From 8 July 2025 (phased per Royal Decree 1007/2023 and the 'Crea y Crece' law 18/2022), all B2B commercial invoices must be issued in structured electronic formats (Facturae, EDIFACT, XML with CII/UBL) and submitted to a certified verification platform ('solución de facturación', e.g., VERI*FACTU interoperability endpoint), affording AEAT near-real-time issuance visibility; QR or digital stamping requirements are platform-certified, not fiscal-stamp based. Maritime towage/salvage operators invoicing the Spanish public sector must additionally use Facturae via the FACe point — invoicing portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to third countries or third territories are zero-rated (exempt with right to deduct input VAT) under Article 21 LIVA, provided the goods physically leave EU territory within the statutory period and are supported by export documentation. Services directly linked to seagoing vessels engaged in international navigation — including maritime towage and salvage services — are zero-rated as international services under Articles 62-63 LIVA (exemption with deduction of input VAT) when the vessel operates on international routes, is engaged in deep-sea towage, or performs salvage in international waters; the shipowner's status and the vessel's tonnage/international navigation certificate must be evidenced. Ancillary services (supply of stores, fuel, crews, and repair services on such vessels) also qualify. Input VAT recovery is available only to the extent the export/international service status is substantiated; intra-Union maritime towage services between Spanish and other EU ports are generally taxable but may be zero-rated where carriage to non-EU destinations is part of one transport chain.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Documento Único Administrativo (DUA) / customs Single Administrative Document (SAD) with export customs declaration and AEAT verification stamp or electronic MRN (Movement Reference Number)
Commercial invoice issued by the Spanish SL with export annotation
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Sea Waybill evidencing departure from an EU port to a non-EU destination
Proof of actual exit of goods from EU customs territory (port authority outward manifest records, Cargo Tracker / ICS declaration, or carrier certification)
Contract or charter party for international towage/salvage engagement, including Lloyds Open Form if applicable
Vessel registration certificate and international navigation evidence (ship's log, Port State Control records)
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT credit confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds within statutory deadlines
If applicable, the AEAT export declaration validation report (Certificado de exportación) and e-export documentation from Customs Single Window
Hunter certificate or assisted salvage agreement where relevant for tug/salvage taxation
Intrastat declaration if goods are moved intra-Union (not required for direct export)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spanish tax authorities (AEAT) and Customs Surveillance place export zero-rating claims under heightened audit scrutiny; documentary insufficiency (missing DUA, bill of lading, or FX repatriation proof within the statutory term) results in retroactive VAT clawback, late-payment interest (interés de demora, monthly rate), and penalty of 50% to 150% of the evaded VAT under Article 191 Ley 58/2003 General Tributaria. Fraudulent or fictitious export zero-rating claims (including sham salvage contracts or circular maritime operations) constitute tax infringement (infracción grave/muy grave) and may trigger criminal prosecution under Article 305 Código Penal where evaded tax exceeds EUR 120,000, with imprisonment of 1 to 5 years, fines of up to six times the evaded amount, and corporate liability sanctions. Additionally, clawback of wrongly deducted input VAT, exclusion from taxpayer top-ranking list (ranking de contribuyentes), and possible suspension of NIF/VAT registration for recurrent abuse are applicable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating under the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy; foreign exchange administration is coordinated with the Secretariat of Commerce and the Directorate-General for International Trade and Investment (Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a Eurozone member; the euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions under EU law (Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Articles 63-66). Profit remittance is unrestricted for EU/EEA residents without prior authorization, subject only to AML/CFT screening and statistical declaration (form SE-130 for transfers exceeding EUR 10,000). For non-EEA investors, capital flows and profit distribution are free unless the operation involves sanctioned jurisdictions, in which case an individual license from the Spanish Ministry of Economy and the CNMV (Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores) may be required under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 and Royal Decree 89/2017.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds in Spain. All export collections invoiced in foreign currency are freely retainable by the exporting entity. However, for statistical and tax control purposes, export invoices must be declared to the Tax Agency (AEAT) within the monthly VAT settlement (Modelo 303) and annual corporate income tax return (Modelo 200), with supporting bank credit evidence. Foreign-currency balances are subject to valuation adjustments at the ECB published exchange rate for tax base calculation (Royal Decree 1065/2007, Article 16). Spanish customs requires the ECS (Export Control System) document and, for transactions above EUR 10,000, additional declaration via BDU (Declaración de Transacciones Económicas).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account - sole business treasury account for towage/salvage clients; can be upgraded to Escrow Account for project-specific contract milestones
Operational Account with multi-currency capability; Capital Escrow Account supported for vessel acquisition or collateralized salvage obligations
Operational Account integrated with maritime financing desk; Escrow Account available for Lloyds Standard Form intermediary settlement
Operational Account with dedicated international desk; Capital Escrow Account for cross-border project advances

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium - Legally feasible for non-EEA fintech EMIs operating under EU payment institution passporting (PSD2) provided the institution holds a valid E/MIR license recognized by the Bank of Spain. EMIs may service operational payments (purchase orders, sub-contractor payments, seafarers' wages) but cannot act as the primary treasury settlement rail for statutory escrow or Lloyds Standard Form salvage awards, as these require a licensed credit institution under Royal Decree Law 1/2007. Furthermore, the Bank of Spain's registration of foreign EMIs is mandatory for any establishment or agent in Spain; non-registered offshore EMIs face service provider blocking under Circular 1/2021.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of all Spanish corporate directors (personas físicas administradores) is generally mandated during initial onboarding at the bank's local branch or via a notarized apostilled mandate presented by a legal representative. Remote opening is accepted only for EU-domiciled directors who hold a valid Spanish or EU identity document and can complete biometric verification through the bank's digital onboarding platform (e.g., Santander SmartBanking, BBVA Remote Onboarding). For non-EEA directors, a physical interview at a Spanish consulate or the bank's overseas subsidiary is mandatory; no fully remote cross-border opening is permitted for an SL entity without an existing EU banking relationship. The Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) registry (BOE 2023) requires all beneficial owners with ≥25% stake to provide passport, proof of address, and source of wealth statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually high invoice amounts for marine salvage without supporting Lloyd's Open Form (LOF) or salvage arbitration award documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Retain fully executed marine salvage contracts, Lloyd's Standard Form of Salvage Agreement (LOF 2020), classification society reports, vessel towage certificates, and a legal opinion from a Spanish maritime law firm confirming commercial substance and fair market valuation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border ownership structure with shareholders in opaque or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide corporate ownership chart, individual UBO passport copies, apostilled certificates of incorporation, audited financial statements for each intermediate holding entity, and a source-of-funds declaration backed by tax filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid movement of funds between the escrow account and multiple sub-contractor bank accounts during a single salvage operation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a project-specific cashflow ledger, subcontractor service agreements with completion certificates, vessel position tracking reports, and a written treasury policy describing segregation of duty for disbursement approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions involving sanctioned vessels or trade routes (e.g., Russian-flagged tugboats or Iranian oil tanker salvage)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Run real-time sanctions screening against OFAC, EU (EU Reg. 269/2014), and UN lists; obtain Lloyds Intelligence vessel ownership and flag history reports; prepare a compliance memo prepared by an external sanctions counsel confirming no circumvention of asset freeze measures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk payment jurisdiction for towage services in West African or South China Sea waters
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Document enhanced due diligence (EDD) file including company registry extract, bank references, business references from local port agents, and ISO 28000 safety management certification; also maintain physical survey reports of the tugboat and salvage gear.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All shareholder capital contributions and investor inflows must be routed via SWIFT MT103 with the correct ISO purpose code. Spain has no requirement to channel capital exclusively through the Bank of Spain; however, for transactions exceeding EUR 10,000, the receiving Spanish bank will report the operation to the Banco de España's Balance of Payments database using the statistical purpose code (e.g., 'P0102' for equity capital, 'P0103' for shareholder loans, 'P0110' for vessel acquisition financing). The SL's escrow account must be designated as a 'Capital Escrow Account' in the corporate treasury agreement, with the following wire memo template: '[Entity EIN] - Equity injection under Escrow Agreement dated [date] - Reference to ISIC 5222 offshore towage/salvage contract [contract number]'. The bank will require a certificate issued by the Spanish Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) confirming the increase in registered capital and the deed granted before a Spanish notary. For foreign currency inbound wires, conversion to EUR is allowed at the ECB-referenced exchange rate or the bank's discretionary dealer rate, subject to the foreign currency being listed on the ECB's official daily reference exchange rates.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Preferred settlement rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 direct credit to the beneficiary's bank for service fees, subcontractor payments, and port disbursement accounts (PDAs); this is the fastest and most transparent route for small-to-medium disbursements under EUR 1 million. (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) in irrevocable documentary credit form (UCP 600) for vessel bunkering, lubricants, crew supplies, and large cargo salvage logistics, where the beneficiary must present a commercial invoice, maritime bill of lading, and a certificate of towage or salvage completion signed by the master. (3) Escrow release instructions under Lloyds Standard Form of Salvage Agreement (Lloyd's Open Form - LOF), requiring the designated escrow bank (typically London-based but acceptable through a Spanish correspondent) to disburse only upon presentation of a salvage arbitration award or an agreement of terms signed by both parties. For payments to sanctioned territories, prior authorization under EU Regulation 833/2014 or a derogation license from the Spanish Ministry of Economy is mandatory before initiating the MT103. All disbursements must be recorded in the Spanish tax ledger and reported via the annual form 415 (annual aggregate foreign payments).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Euro/US Dollar forward outright contracts (FX forwards) transacted with an authorized Spanish credit institution, maximum tenor 12 months, no margin leverage beyond standard bilateral credit line

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/NOK) used solely to align revenue streams from foreign salvage contracts with the entity's euro-denominated operating costs; requires ISDA master agreement with CSA collateral

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible on an exceptional basis for emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, NGN, BRL) where local FX controls prevent physical delivery; prohibited for use as speculative trading instruments
Spot FX forward options embedded in the corporate foreign-exchange policy, capped at notional 200% of expected contract cashflows
Commodity-linked hedges for marine diesel (bunker fuel) are outside the FX hedging scope but may be executed via approved ISDA/MMRA confirmations and reported under IFRS 9 hedge accounting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the annual accounts by the General Meeting of Shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of 1,500-3,000 EUR, potential dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25 July following the end of the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of 100-500 EUR per day of delay, plus surcharges and interest

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Net turnover exceeding 2,000,000 EUR, total assets exceeding 1,000,000 EUR, or average number of employees exceeding 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) or IFRS where consolidated reporting applies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual confirmation required; notify any changes in beneficial ownership or control to the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales within one month

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% CIT rate for newly created S.L. during the first two taxable years of qualifying economic activity; R&D and technological innovation tax credits (25%-42%); patent box regime (9.5% on qualifying IP income); international double-taxation relief; capitalisation reserve and SME preferential deductions. No outright statutory tax holiday applies to offshore towage and salvage activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically through the AEAT Sede Electrónica; Modelo 202 for quarterly prepayments; Modelo 222 for consolidated groups; Form 216 annual withholding summary for dividends and interest paid to non-residents; Modelo 232 related-party transaction disclosure.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Modelo 200 must be filed within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year S.L., the filing window is 1-25 July. Quarterly prepayments are due 1-20 April, 1-20 July, 1-20 October, and 1-20 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result before corporate income tax, computed from audited or statutory financial statements; includes all income from global towage and salvage contracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident Spanish S.L. is the taxpayer; non-resident beneficial owners are not shown in this field, but must be disclosed as UBOs where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary adjustments to the accounting result, including arm's-length corrections, disallowed expenses, depreciation recapture and capitalisation reserve adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign related parties, such as charter hire, crew subcontractor fees, management fees and royalties, must be adequately documented and aligned to the arm's-length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year negative taxable bases against current taxable income, subject to statutory annual compensation limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforwards are attributes of the Spanish S.L.; a non-resident shareholder acquiring the company must verify historical loss use and continuity of business activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after loss compensation, before deductions and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the general 25% rate, or 15% if the S.L. validly qualifies as newly created; non-resident ownership alone does not alter the entity-level CIT rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and deductions: R&D credit, job creation credit, international economic double-taxation credit, withholding tax credits and treaty credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: These credits are used by the S.L.; distributions to non-resident shareholders remain separately subject to Spanish withholding tax under IRNR and applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refund due, after quarterly prepayments and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the S.L. fails to withhold on dividends paid to non-residents, the company may be held liable as the withholding substitute taxpayer.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT notification triggers a graduated surcharge: 5% within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% thereafter, plus daily late-payment interest. Filing after notification or non-filing exposes the company to proportional penalties of 50%-150% of the tax deficiency; incomplete Form 232 or withholding forms trigger fixed recurring fines and statutory interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% under Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR); 0% under the EU/EEA Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying parent holdings of at least 5% held for one year or more; treaty-reduced rates generally range from 0% to 15% depending on ownership percentage and residence jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident recipient must prove beneficial ownership and tax residence. Submit to the Spanish paying S.L. the current Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, together with certified ownership history and, where applicable, parent-subsidiary evidence. If reduced treaty withholding was not applied at source, the recipient must file Modelo 210 and claim a refund within the statutory limitation period, generally four years, attaching the TRC, distribution resolution, payment confirmation and legalisation documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates for non-residents without a Spanish permanent establishment are 19% for interest and 19% for royalties. Treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 10% for interest and 5% to 10% for royalties. Under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, exemption can apply to connected companies holding 25% or more for at least two years, subject to anti-abuse and economic substance checks.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 45,000,000 annual net turnover triggers mandatory full Local File and Master File documentation. Form 232 must be filed where related-party transactions with the same related entity exceed EUR 100,000 or satisfy other materiality thresholds. Groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750,000,000 must file Country-by-Country Reporting via Modelo 231.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations filing regime. Instead, substance is enforced through Article 13 of the LGT (legal reality), Article 15 of the LIS as a general anti-abuse rule, CFC provisions in Article 100 LIS, beneficial ownership doctrine and DTA anti-abuse clauses. An offshore towage and salvage S.L. must evidence genuine activity in Spain: board decisions, vessel ownership and operation control, crew employment, local contracts, invoicing and real assets. Without such substance, the entity may be recharacterised as a shell and treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and concealment of towage and salvage revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Systematically omitting contract revenue from deep-sea tug services, diverting salvage payments to foreign personal accounts, issuing false invoices for fuel, crew wages and port services, or accumulating unjustified cash write-offs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50%-150% of the tax evaded plus late-payment interest. Criminal liability under Article 305 Penal Code arises where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000: imprisonment of two to six years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced for fraud, mixed assets or abuse; directors, shadow directors and signatories are jointly and severally liable for tax restitution, and may be subject to travel bans, asset seizures, disqualification and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a minimum-capital S.L. as a pure invoicing or asset-holding conduit for non-resident principals, with no crew, no owned or operated vessels, no Spanish office, no board decision-making and no operating substance, while profits are shifted to a zero-tax or no-tax offshore affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation under GAAR, CFC rules and beneficial ownership tests; deductions for shifted payments are disallowed, the tax base is recalculated at 25%, and penalties of 50%-150% apply. Treaty relief may be denied under the Principal Purpose Test and economic substance requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false financial statements, appoint nominee directors, or conceal the actual overseas principal may be held civilly liable for the full CIT deficiency; criminal courts may impose restitution, travel bans and imprisonment for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing documentation and arm's-length failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare the Local File and Master File, omitting Modelo 232 disclosure, or charging non-arm's-length rates for intercompany towage, salvage, charter hire, insurance or management services between the Spanish S.L. and a foreign related party.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may make a transfer-pricing adjustment plus daily late-payment interest; material documentation omissions trigger recurring fixed penalties, and any resulting tax deficiency attracts a proportional penalty of 50%-150%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: CFO, finance directors and tax representatives who certify incomplete or misleading TP documentation can be personally joint-liable for the tax deficiency; deliberate false documentation supports criminal tax fraud charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties, shareholder interest, consultancy fees or charter fees to the non-resident parent in amounts that economically represent dividends, without genuine service performance, genuine debt documentation, or arm's-length pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation as constructive dividend under IRNR; the Spanish payer is liable for 19% withholding tax plus penalties of 50%-150% and late interest; if fraud is proven, criminal tax penalties also attach.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving unsupported distributions or circular invoices may have personal liability for unpaid withholding and civil restitution; where the arrangement is fraudulent, directors face travel bans, disqualification and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and ultimate beneficial owner concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Hiding the true non-resident beneficial owner behind nominees, bearer instruments or trusts; failing to register UBO details in the Registro Mercantil; accepting cash or unidentifiable payments for high-value salvage contracts; operating bank accounts with opaque or undeclared sources of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 10/2010, very serious AML violations can produce fines up to EUR 1,000,000 or a percentage of the serviced volume; criminal money laundering under Article 301 Penal Code carries imprisonment of six months to six years, fines, confiscation and possible corporate liquidation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Designated compliance officers and directors may be personally fined and criminally sanctioned; veil-piercing allows the tax authority and creditors to reach personal assets; travel bans and forfeiture orders commonly accompany money-laundering convictions.
